thread:
Jamie: Heads up — since yesterday's batching/kernel patch we've seen intermittent 200-800ms tail latency spikes on kv-heavy long-context requests. mostly on a subset of prod-gpu-4 nodes :confused:
Sandeep: saw that. correlates with high kv-pages-in and eviction counts. looks like eviction policy is flipping between FIFO and LRU behavior under pressure. can repro on staging with long-context-80k test.
Tess: any error logs? OOMs?
Jamie: no OOMs. but memory for kv arena grows steadily during a single long session, then huge pause when reclaim happens. stack traces show pager thread getting busy. quick logs:```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] kv: allocate shard=3 sz=6.2MB
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] kv: eviction:start shard=3 policy=FIFO candidates=128
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] kv: page-in shard=3 seq=98532
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] kv: eviction:reinsert shard=3 key=0x7f9a23b cnt=1
[2026-03-15T08:12:04Z] perf: token-latency p90=83ms p99=420ms
```
Maria: interesting — eviction:reinsert line stands out. we added a fifo reinsert optimization in the fallback path to avoid churn, but if reinsert ordering interacts with ongoing reads it could cause extra page churn.
Sandeep: I profiled a repro run; flame graph shows heavy time in kv::reclaim_loop and kernelSelector waiting on cudaMemcpy for paging. batching looks fine; kernel selection isn't the culprit here. attaching quick profile id: profile-19421-a (staging).
Jamie: repro steps I used:```
# run long-context harness
./tools/long_context_load.sh --model rwd-mid --seq 60000 --concurrency 6 --workload kv-heavy
```
and then tail node logs.
Tess: can we toggle the fifo fallback off in staging and see if spike goes away?
Maria: toggled FIFO_REINSERT=false on canary, rolling 2 nodes now.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for flag FIFO_REINSERT -> false on pool prod-gpu-4-canary (2/24 nodes).
Sandeep: initial canary looks promising: p99 down from 420ms -> 95ms on those two nodes. still seeing occasional micro-spikes (30-60ms) but nothing like before.
Jamie: good. root cause hypothesis: fifo reinsert didn't account for concurrent reuse pointers so items get reinserted at tail while hot readers keep touching them causing a loop of page-ins and evictions (cache thrash) until the reclaim watermark triggers a big pause.
Tess: are there correctness concerns (stale reuse pointers / double-free)?
Sandeep: I checked memory accounting and no leaks, but there is a race window where reinserted entries are considered 'cold' by the FIFO walker while ongoing lookups update their last-used generation — the arithmetic for generation aging is off by one. smells like off-by-one bug in aging epoch increment.
Maria: proposals: 1) revert fifo reinsert optimization (we're doing that on canary) 2) add a per-shard lightweight pin counter to prevent eviction while an entry is actively being read 3) update metrics to expose "reinsert_count" and "reinsert_collision" and alert when reinsert_collision > 50/min 4) add unit/integration test that simulates concurrent lookup+reinsert under pressure.
Jamie: +1 on metrics and tests. pin counter seems safe but may add small overhead. I prefer incremental: revert now, add metrics/tests, then reintroduce reinsert with pin or atomic generation bump.
Tess: I'll own the revert and can follow up with a patch to add reinsert metrics. Jamie, can you assemble minimal repro test for CI?
Jamie: yes — will push harness and a tiny e2e test that hits the exact timing window. also adding an opt-in stress_test that runs for 5min.
Sandeep: for long-term: consider hybrid policy: LRU eviction within hot window, FIFO for cold regions, and explicit aging window updates on reads. Might remove the reinsert code entirely and rely on smarter eviction watermarks.
Maria: also add telemetry events for "evict_policy_flip" so we can detect policy oscillation across nodes and rollouts.
Jamie: created GH issue rwd/infra#2149 with logs and initial plan.
Tess: cheers. canary looked stable for 15m, rolling out revert to rest of pool now. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollout completed for flag FIFO_REINSERT -> false on pool prod-gpu-4 (24/24 nodes).
Sandeep: after full rollback p99 stabilised to ~80-100ms. leaving monitoring on for 24h.
Maria: nice work. next steps: tests + metrics + design doc for hybrid eviction. assign owners? Jamie (test + repro), Tess (rollback + metrics), Sandeep (design doc + profiling).
Jamie: will also add note to changelog about eviction semantics change and link to the scheduling heuristics doc.
Tess: thanks everyone. follow-up sync tomorrow 9:30am PT for the design doc draft. :calendar:
